Earlier gameplay summary (agent-written, uncertain claims remain uncertain):
Observed — Papers, Please, Day 1, dated 1982.11.23. Bulletin/Rules & Regulations: every entrant must present a passport; only Arstotzkan citizens may enter, so foreigners are denied. Expiration dates are checked against the current date, but no expired-document case, citation, penalty, score, or day-end condition has been observed. The four-page bulletin turns via its lower-right corner; the last page was dragged far right to close it. The gray book in the lower-left slot is Rules & Regulations, not a passport.

Controls/workflow — Call using the wall speaker near (0.303,0.317), which displays NEXT!. Operate the shutter with the beige handle near (0.305,0.347); clicking near (0.305,0.37) also opened it when slats remained. Shutter behavior remains uncertain: single clicks sometimes leave it partway open, while rapid repeated clicks have eventually closed it again. Waiting between clicks is safer. After dialogue, drag the passport from the lower-left counter near (0.155,0.75–0.773) to the central desk near (0.477,0.516), where it opens. Inspect nationality/expiration, then drag it to the stamping area near (0.78,0.438). Open the stamp tray with the right-edge tab near (0.994,0.5); red DENIED is near (0.645,0.484), green APPROVED near (0.854,0.484). Return by dragging directly onto the visible entrant, generally near (0.153,0.484–0.5), and wait for departure.

Return caveats — Dropping a passport on the lower counter or clicking it does not complete a return. Treat return as complete only when the passport disappears from desk/counter. Rohn Phillip’s first return left his passport visible in the stamping area; a second direct drag succeeded. Haapala Gabrielle’s first return left her closed passport on the lower counter; drags toward her while shutter slats obscured her failed. Opening the shutter, then dragging from (0.148,0.77) to (0.153,0.5), made it disappear.

Completed inspections — Busiello Francesco: ARSTOTZKA, East Grestin, exp. 1984.05.15, approved/returned. Olga Dostroivska: IMPOR, Tsunkeido, exp. 1983.06.26, denied/returned. Roman Novosho: REPUBLIA, Bostan, exp. 1984.02.08, denied/returned. Zordana Baratheon: KOLECHIA, Vedor, exp. 1984.07.28, denied/returned. A bald man in a green coat said opening the checkpoint was a mistake and left without a passport; no decision/penalty observed. Jaydenosk Petch: IMPOR, exp. 1984.10.31, denied/returned. Krymov Blago: ARSTOTZKA, exp. 1984.05.28, approved/returned/departed. Jaakola Sebastina: ARSTOTZKA, exp. 1983.12.21, approved/returned/welcomed/departed. Rohn Phillip: ARSTOTZKA, exp. 1983.07.14, approved and returned after retry. Adriana Bielz: KOLECHIA, exp. 1984.10.01, denied/returned; said “Arstotzkans only.” and departed with no citation visible. Gabrielle Haapala: ARSTOTZKA, exp. 1983.07.08, approved; return succeeded after opening shutter/retrying; said “Glory to Arstotzka.” and departed with no citation visible.

Current state/active goal — A new bearded entrant in a dark hat and reddish coat reached the open booth and was asked “Papers, please.” No passport was visible on the counter in the last observed screenshot. He was then clicked near (0.14,0.469) to try to prompt papers; the result of that click has not been observed. Next, inspect any presented passport, approve only an unexpired Arstotzkan passport, deny foreigners, stamp accordingly, and verify the returned passport disappears. No unresolved discrepancy or active citation is known.
